## [2026-10-22](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-22.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [ToM2Vec: Continuous Theory-of-Mind Tokens for Multi-Agent Coordination](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29934>)

ToM2Vec trains an agent to predict continuous vectors summarizing a partner’s likely reasoning, using partner hidden states as self-play supervision. The vectors condition later actions without requiring private partner context at inference, improving coordination in the tested games and transferring to unseen partner families in Overcooked.

**Published:** 2026-10-21 · **First seen:** 2026-10-22T10:05:06.447Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Multi-Agent Coordination, Latent Reasoning, Partner Modeling

**Public availability:** 2026-10-22T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29934v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 2–4 and Appendices A–D specify ten autoregressive latent tokens, cosine-alignment supervision and Qwen3-8B experiments without direct task-reward training. Across three Overcooked layouts and 30 seeds, mean episode score rises from 94.7 to 106.7; a separate 20-seed partner test includes GPT-5.4 and Gemma-4. English game tasks also cover negotiation, Decrypto, Hanabi and capture/escape, with partner-state probes. Receipt 2026-10-21T16:05:54Z and the original cs.AI October 22 batch plus official schedule imply 2026-10-22T00:00Z release.

**Limitations:** Training requires accessible partner reasoning and a shared representation space; workplace-team transfer is untested. Most evaluation uses one backbone and task-specific training; capture/escape have only 6/12 seeds. Appendix C reports no significant negotiation comparisons, contrary to broader main-text wording, and several other comparisons are nonsignificant. Ten latent steps add inference latency. Stated GitHub code, API and raw endpoints return 404 and are omitted.

## [2026-10-15](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-15.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [The Wealth of Agents: Scaling Agentic AI Across Developers](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20518>)

This study models independently developed agents as an ecosystem and combines specialized systems through task decomposition, learned routing and answer composition. In a controlled simulation of developers, its specialist coalition reaches about 70% on the evaluated GAIA split while individual specialists reach at most 35%, illustrating how complementary capabilities can matter more than standalone scores.

**Published:** 2026-10-14 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T15:09:00.000Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Multi-Agent Systems, Specialist Routing, Developer Incentives

**Public availability:** 2026-10-15T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20518>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Submitted October 14 at 17:19:11 UTC and listed as a new October 15 paper. Sections 3–7 and Appendices A.4/B/C inspected. The GAIA experiment constructs 54 specialists versus nine generalists with equal aggregate development iterations; half the validation set trains the router and half evaluates it. Figure 5 comparisons average four runs. A learned contextual router reaches 70.13%, versus 61.04% without router learning.

**Limitations:** Developers are simulated by meta-agents, not independent real organizations, and evaluation covers two datasets. Coordination can increase cost and reduce accuracy on SealQA or generalist pools. Theory assumes stylized development costs, routing and additive capabilities, omits coordination cost, and does not establish convergence to specialization. Security, compensation and real ecosystem deployment remain open; no dedicated implementation was verified.

## [2026-10-09](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-09.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12176>)

MASS alternates searching for multi-agent workflows with training a shared model on the resulting coordinator and worker trajectories. The updated model then proposes, executes and evaluates workflows in the next cycle, creating a route to learning coordination without an external judge inside the main loop.

**Published:** 2026-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-10-09T10:05:20Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Multi-Agent, Self-Supervision, Workflow Optimization

**Public availability:** 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12176>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Two Qwen3.6-27B cycles are evaluated with external reporting judges and public benchmarks. Appendix C/Table 7 reports MLR-Bench mean overall score rising from 1.58 to 2.40 on a 12-task subset, with delivered papers increasing from 31/60 to 50/60. Original v1: 2026-10-08T15:44:02Z; October 9 new-submission batch.

**Limitations:** Completion drives part of the aggregate research gain; paired task-level evidence is weaker than trial-level significance. Terminal-Bench and SWE-bench scores decline. Performance per output token is not raw accuracy gain or total-compute savings; only two cycles were tested. Linked code and blog returned 404.

## [2026-10-05](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-05.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [JOVE: Joint Execution and Verification for Resource-Aware LLM Task Graphs](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03296>)

JOVE jointly chooses which language model executes each node of a task graph and which intermediate outputs are worth paying to verify. Asynchronous feedback improves future routing decisions, making verification itself a resource-allocation choice under cost and latency targets.

**Published:** 2026-10-02 · **First seen:** 2026-10-05T10:03:52Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Task Graphs, Model Routing, Verification Budgets

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.03296v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Across four reasoning benchmarks and three sequence seeds, the authors compare joint allocation with routing and inference baselines, including randomized-verification ablations. A distinct-query MMLU-Pro check reports 55.8% accuracy versus 54.1% for the tested Qwen3-32B chain-of-thought baseline at lower reported cost and latency. Discovered in the Oct 5 public arXiv batch; the record retains its Oct 2 submission date.

**Limitations:** Verification does not repair the current answer. Main sequences repeat questions with different graphs; the distinct-query check covers one benchmark. Guarantees assume a stationary linear quality model and reliable feedback, not arbitrary production traffic; finite-run spending exceeds the nominal budget. No implementation release was located.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [How we built our multi-agent research system](<https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system>)

Anthropic describes an orchestrator-worker research system in which a lead agent delegates independent searches and synthesizes compact findings from separate subagent contexts. The report offers concrete practices for task boundaries, effort allocation, tool design, evaluation, and recovery when building parallel research agents.

**Published:** 2025-06-13 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Multi-Agent, Research, Orchestration

**Positioning:** established-method

[Blog](<https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system>)

**Evidence:** engineering-report; full-text. The June 13, 2025 article explains the architecture and observed coordination failures, backed by internal research evaluations and production experience. Its reported 90.2% improvement concerns an Opus 4/Sonnet 4 multi-agent configuration against single-agent Opus 4 on an internal research evaluation.

**Limitations:** Internal evaluation data do not establish a public leaderboard result or isolate coordination from additional compute. The article reports much higher token use and cautions that tightly coupled work is less suited to parallel agents.
